title: Implement a thread-safe word frequency counter
question: Write a Java method that counts word occurrences in a text using ConcurrentHashMap and LongAdder.
explanation: computeIfAbsent creates one LongAdder per word, and LongAdder supports efficient concurrent increments. The result map is a snapshot after input processing completes.
complexity: Expected O(n) time for n words; O(u) space for u distinct words.

title: Find the third-highest distinct salary
question: Given a list of employees, find the third-highest distinct salary using Java Streams.
explanation: Map employees to salaries, remove duplicates, sort descending, skip the first two distinct values, and return the next. Optional.empty() is returned if fewer than three distinct salaries exist.
complexity: O(n log n) time due to sorting; O(n) additional space.

title: Check whether two strings are isomorphic
question: Write a Java program to determine whether two strings are isomorphic: each character in one string must map consistently to one character in the other.
explanation: Two maps enforce a one-to-one mapping in both directions. For example, egg and add are isomorphic, while foo and bar are not.
complexity: O(n) time and O(k) space, where k is the number of distinct characters.

title: Find the longest subarray with sum K
question: Given an integer array that may contain negative values, find the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum equals K.
explanation: Store the earliest index for each prefix sum. If prefixSum - K has appeared, the elements between that index and the current index sum to K. This works with negative numbers too.
complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Search in a row-wise and column-wise sorted matrix
question: Find a target in a matrix where every row and every column is sorted in ascending order.
explanation: Start at the top-right corner. A value that is too large eliminates its column; a value that is too small eliminates its row.
complexity: O(rows + columns) time and O(1) extra space.

title: Merge two sorted singly linked lists
question: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list by reusing existing nodes.
explanation: A dummy head simplifies edge cases. Each iteration appends the smaller current node; the remaining list is attached at the end.
complexity: O(m + n) time and O(1) extra space, excluding the reused nodes.

title: Find the minimum number of coins for an amount
question: Given coin denominations and an amount, find the minimum number of coins needed. Assume unlimited coins and return -1 if the amount cannot be formed.
explanation: dp[x] stores the fewest coins needed for amount x. For every amount, try using each valid denomination as the final coin.
complexity: O(amount × numberOfCoins) time and O(amount) space.

title: Partition employees into salary bands
question: Using Java Streams, group employees into two groups: salary at least a threshold and salary below the threshold.
explanation: Collectors.partitioningBy always creates true and false partitions. The true key represents employees whose salary is greater than or equal to the threshold.
complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the collected lists.

title: Validate balanced brackets of three types
question: Write a Java program to validate whether (), {}, and [] are correctly balanced and nested.
explanation: Push opening brackets. For every closing bracket, pop and verify its matching opener. The stack must be empty at the end.

title: Check whether a number is a power of two
question: Write a Java method that checks whether a positive integer is a power of two.
explanation: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit in binary. Subtracting one clears that bit and sets lower bits, so n & (n - 1) equals zero.
